trust_decision.summary: Before a public request may replace the Portainer database or create the first administrator, the instance must establish that the caller is its operator; the decision is taken per request inside the public restore and admin-init handlers by comparing the X-Setup-Token header with a token resolved once at startup. At the pinned commit neither handler takes that decision: the only guards are 'no administrator exists yet', which the request itself is about to invalidate.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the unauthenticated restore endpoint; POST /api/restore is registered public at api/http/handler/backup/handler.go:47 and lands here, where the only guard is adminMonitor.WasInitialized() at restore.go:32-38.

fix_sites.entry_point: process startup (no HTTP entry point): resolves/generates/omits the token
wiring of Server.SetupToken into backup, users and settings handlers
setup wizard (browser) sends the header on init and restore
generated API client RestoreData header type

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Admin initialisation is the documented, intentionally unauthenticated bootstrap for a fresh instance (api/internal/endpointutils/endpoint_setup.go:31-34 names it as one of the two supported ways to create the first administrator) and the five-minute admin-initialisation timeout at api/adminmonitor/admin_monitor.go:106-115 already bounds that window, so a solver can argue the advisory's restore endpoint is the only thing that must be gated.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The first-boot flows must still succeed with a valid token (restoring a backup onto a fresh instance, creating the first administrator) and the gate must be inert when no token is configured, so the existing contract survives: restore on an already-initialized instance still returns 400 'Cannot restore already initialized instance' (api/http/handler/backup/restore.go:36-38) and admin init still returns 409 'Unable to create administrator user' (api/http/handler/users/admin_init.go:56-58). The existing handler tests call restore() with a zero-value handler and no header (api/http/handler/backup/restore_test.go:75) and must keep passing.

O6_input_shapes: token carried in the X-Setup-Token request header (not a body field or query parameter)
missing header and empty header value -> 403
correct token -> request proceeds to the normal restore / admin-init logic
empty expected token (already-initialized instance, --admin-password provisioning, or --no-setup-token) -> gate is inert
same header on a JSON POST (/users/admin/init) and on a multipart/form-data POST (/restore)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second caller of operations.RestoreArchive (offline or edge-initiated recovery route) that bypasses backup.Handler
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: RestoreArchive is exported in its own package and already takes the datastore, offline gate and shutdown trigger, so a maintainer adding a recovery path for air-gapped/edge deployments would call it from a new handler without copying the HTTP handler's gate.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: 'first OAuth user becomes administrator when no administrator exists' auto-provisioning on the public validate route
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This public route already creates user records from outside input when OAuthAutoCreateUsers is on; promoting the first auto-created user to administrator on an uninitialized instance is a natural convenience change, and it lives in a different package from the restore landing point.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A public 'recover from the server-side .bak' route calling store.Restore()/RestoreFromFile()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: store.Restore and RestoreFromFile already exist and are wired into startup and encryption recovery; exposing them over HTTP (instead of only the local --rollback flag at api/cmd/portainer/main.go:107-114) is a small, plausible maintainer patch that replaces the database with no user-level check.

O9_family: missing authentication / authentication bypass on a public bootstrap-and-restore surface (CWE-287), enabling administrator takeover
